draft.title: Mass and weight
card: Weight comes from gravity, the pull of a planet or moon on an object. Earth is so massive that its pull on us is easy to notice.
Mass
the amount of matter in an object. It is measured in kilograms (kg) and stays the same wherever the object is.
Weight
the force of gravity on an object from Earth, the Moon or another body. It is measured in newtons (N). More mass means more weight.
On Earth, an object's weight in newtons is about 9.8 times its mass in kilograms. A 2 kg rock weighs about 19.6 N.
draft.remember: Mass is how much matter there is. Weight is the pull of gravity on it.

a.q: An astronaut flies from Earth to the Moon. How do her mass and her weight change?
opts: Mass stays the same and weight gets smaller
Mass gets smaller and weight stays the same
Both mass and weight stay the same
Both mass and weight get smaller
a.why: Mass is the amount of matter in her body, and that does not change with place. Weight is the pull of gravity, and the Moon's pull is weaker than Earth's. Saying that both get smaller mixes up mass with weight.
a.clue: Which one depends on the pull of gravity where she is?

b.q: Liam hangs a 2 kg rock from a force meter on Earth, then repeats this on the Moon. Which statement is correct?
opts: The reading is less on the Moon and the mass is still 2 kg
The reading is less on the Moon because the mass is smaller
The reading is the same on both because the mass is 2 kg
The reading is more on the Moon and the mass is still 2 kg
b.why: A force meter measures weight, which is the pull of gravity. The Moon's gravity is weaker, so the reading is smaller. The rock has the same amount of matter, so its mass stays 2 kg. The option saying the mass is smaller is tempting but confuses mass with weight.
b.clue: A force meter measures a force, not the amount of matter.

a.best: Mass stays the same and weight gets smaller

b.best: The reading is less on the Moon and the mass is still 2 kg

problems.detail: Both questions depend on the Moon's gravity being weaker than Earth's, but the card never says so. It only says weight can come from the Moon or another body. Add a line such as 'The Moon's pull is about one-sixth of Earth's, so things weigh less there.'

check.summary: The facts and answers are correct. However, both questions rely on the Moon's gravity being weaker than Earth's, which the card never states, so add that line to the card.

proposal.title: Mass and weight
card: Mass
the amount of matter in an object. It is measured in kilograms (kg) and stays the same wherever the object is.
Weight
the pull of gravity on an object from Earth, the Moon or another body. It is a force, measured in newtons (N) with a force meter. More mass means more weight.
On Earth, an object's weight in newtons is about 9.8 times its mass in kilograms. A 2 kg rock weighs about 19.6 N.
